neighbours.label: the punctuation or conjunction right after a word used as a mention ('words like not or never', 'the word X,') or closing an unquoted 'he thought'
fire: Writers should avoid hedges like perhaps or somewhat in a conclusion.
Prefer short verbs such as cut or fix over their noun forms.

In this manual the term operator
means the person who holds the licence.
Fillers like basically or literally weaken a speech.
Nobody will notice, Ellen thought, if I leave through the garden.
It is already too late, he thought again, and sat back down.
The word robot, as Čapek coined it, meant forced labour.
Use whom, not who, after a preposition in formal prose.
quiet: Writers should avoid hedging in a conclusion.
Prefer short verbs over long noun phrases.
In this manual the operator is the person who holds the licence.
Fillers weaken a speech more than silence does.
"Nobody will notice if I leave through the garden," Ellen said.
It was already too late, and he sat back down.
The robot, as Čapek imagined it, was a forced labourer.
Use a preposition before the relative pronoun in formal prose.
